newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian securitisation to increase - PUMA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian securitisation to increase - PUMA.

text.p: Securitised funding and non-bank mortage managers should continue to grow their market share of the Australian home lending market, according to Macquarie Bank's securitisation arm, PUMA management Ltd.
PUMA, Australia's largest non-bank securitiser, believes that Australia would follow the U.S.'s lead where non-bank origninators hold some 45 percent of the total mortgage market.

"In Australia, we estimate that 20 to 30 percent of the mortgage market -- both bank and non-bank originated -- may ultimately by funded by securitisation," Andrew Bruce, Associate Director at PUMA told a seminar in Sydney.

Bruce said that new mortgage products and features, a greater penetration into non-mortgage asset classes, changing consumer buying habits and new capital market instruments may feature in the industry's near future.
However, he added that competitive fall-out is also likely to occur.
"Second tier banks, credit unions and similar orgainsations may find themselves strategically 'stuck-in-the-middle', that is having neither critical mass, cost advantages nor cheap funding," he said.
"These players may find themselves fiercely squeezed on their traditional home turf with an uncertain competitive response," Bruce added.

On the major banks, Bruce said that they have the ability to use securitisation to fund their own portfolios, driven by both cost of funds and balance sheet efficiency, and will provide significant volume into the MBS market.

"Investors, having developed an interest in mortgage backed issues, will now become more discerning. Securitisers will need to create securities that are clearly attractive to investors, and which meet their risk, payment and pricing requirements."

Bruce also saw global issues becoming more common with securitisation vehicles accessing both Australian and international investor bases, while Australian investors may also gain increasing access to international assets.
"Securitisers will need to ensure their on-going asset supply and create bonds which are internationally attractive and cost effective," he said.
Finally Bruce said that the mortgage market had witnessed a permanent realignment. "Home loan funding is, and will remain, cheaper, because of securitisation," he added.
